claim: s↦1−s symmetry alone does NOT force RH (no Euler product)
measured: L(−2, χ₋₄) = -800000000.0 (a zero of a series satisfying a Riemann-type FE), and multiplicativity can fail outright: a(2)a(3) = 0 ≠ a(6) = 0
detail: The load-bearing ingredient for RH is the EULER PRODUCT (multiplicativity), not the functional equation. Davenport–Heilbronn is the standard counterexample: a genuine s ↔ 1−s functional equation with PROVEN zeros off Re s = 1/2, because it has no Euler product. Conversely Epstein zeta functions share the symmetry and have off-line zeros. The corpus states this correctly and it is its sharpest RH insight.
notes: the corpus' own HSLNZeta.lean docstring says exactly this: 'The symmetry ALONE does not force the zeros onto the line: Epstein zeta functions and the Davenport–Heilbronn function have the SAME s<->1-s functional equation yet have zeros OFF the critical line, because they lack an Euler product (the prime structure).'

detail: sin(πx/p) vanishes exactly at multiples of p, so the product vanishes exactly on the composites with a prime factor ≤ 7. Every composite n ≤ 100 has a prime factor ≤ √100 = 10, so the survivors in (7,100] are exactly the primes. Correct — and it is exactly trial division by {2,3,5,7}.
notes: the corpus calls this 'a blind cheerful attempt that works'; it is a re-encoding of the classical sieve, not a new primality test. The detector primes themselves are necessarily killed by the product, which is why the test starts above 7.
